text:
Judd Caulfield was a fifth-round pick in 2019, spent last season scoring 38 points in 71 AHL games for San Diego, and only now, at 25, made an NHL opening-night roster. The North Dakota kid has nine points in 15 games for Anaheim, four of them on the power play, and his ice time has climbed about three minutes over the last ten.

How much of it is real? More than you'd guess. His own chances are strong, 1.51 expected goals per 60, and his 5v5 impact relative to teammates is positive. He's also been on the right side of some on-ice luck (2.68 goals above expected) and his 20 percent shooting will not last. Our range has him near 47 points over a full season, with a wide spread around it.

He plays a physical, net-front style (51 hits already) that fits a team suddenly winning games. The three-point night against Ottawa, when he and Cutter Gauthier combined for five goals, was the headline. The steady part is the chances.
headline: Caulfield waited six years for this
